name: BNP Paribas

particularites.text: Legacy state shareholdings stemming from the 2008 financial crisis and the Fortis rescue: Societe Federale de Participations et d'Investissement (Belgian State, ~5,7% of the share capital) and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg (~1,1%) - stable long-term shareholders, with no reported active governance role and no impact on the projections.

ownership.insiderDesc: Employee shareholding ~4,3% of the share capital (standard employee savings/share ownership schemes of a large French banking group, no significant individual management holding reported). Treasury shares ~1,5%. Institutional ownership is very much the majority and diversified: European institutional investors 41,5%, foreign institutional investors 31,7%, individual shareholders 7,2%, BlackRock 7,0% (passive position). No single controlling shareholder; standard listed-bank governance with no founding family.
ownership.insiderSource: ABC Bourse - company profile (shareholder breakdown), cross-checked against the standard governance profile of large listed French banks
ownership.coverageNote: No tier-1 watchlist investor identified with a notable position in this stock. BlackRock (7,0%) is a standard passive institutional position, outside the scope of the named watchlist.

items.title: Civil litigation in the United States tied to BNP Paribas's role in financing Sudanese entities between the late 1990s and 2009 (letters of credit on oil/agricultural contracts): a Manhattan federal jury found the Bank liable in October 2025 for having helped the Sudanese regime commit abuses by violating US sanctions, ordering BNP Paribas to pay 20,5 M$ of damages to three Sudanese plaintiffs. Certification of the verdict (7 January 2026) opens the way to an appeal, already lodged by the Bank (motion filed in early February 2026). Plaintiffs' lawyers point to a potential extension to a class of ~23 000 Sudanese refugees claiming far higher amounts.
items.allegedBy: Sudanese plaintiffs (individuals, via a potential class action) before a Manhattan federal court
items.outcome: 20,5 M$ of damages to three plaintiffs (first instance); appeal under way, outcome unknown
items.source: Communiques officiels BNP Paribas (28/10/2025, 08/01/2026) + presse (Reuters, Boursorama, AllAfrica)

items.title: BNP Paribas guilty plea for conspiracy to violate US sanctions (Sudan, Cuba, Iran, 2004-2012) - landmark ~8,9 Md$ settlement with the US authorities (DOJ, Federal Reserve, State of New York, OFAC).
items.allegedBy: US Department of Justice (DOJ) and US banking regulators
items.outcome: Fine/settlement of ~8,9 Md$, guilty plea accepted
items.source: Official DOJ press release (justice.gov, archives), extensively documented publicly - mentioned here as historical context for the still-active Sudan litigation

compliance.note: The 2014 case is closed (settlement paid more than ten years ago) and mentioned only as context for the still-active Sudan civil litigation, which is the real point of caution for this refresh/creation. No other securities fraud allegation identified at this stage.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quantified quarterly guidance published (banking convention, annual/multi-year guidance only).
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: 2026 targets confirmed unchanged: ROTE 12%, attributable net income CAGR >7% and EPS CAGR >8% over 2024-2026, revenue CAGR >5% over 2024-2026, jaws effect ~+1,5 pt/yr on average, cost of risk <40 basis points. 2028 targets confirmed (raised in February 2026): ROTE >13%, cost/income ratio <56%, attributable net income CAGR >10% over 2025-2028, post-FRTB CET1 ratio at 13% at 31/12/2027 AND at 31/12/2028 (already reached ahead of schedule at 30/06/2026 at 13,0%).
pointsCles: Q2 net income group share of EUR 4,345M (+33.4% y/y, above the ~EUR 4.2B consensus) on revenue of EUR 14,091M (+12%, a growth rate 'not seen for a decade'); the quarter includes an ~EUR 858M capital gain on the Ageas/AG Insurance disposal (non-operating, excluded from omniumNet) which also adds ~EUR 0.50/share to distribution and ~EUR 40M of recurring earnings from 2027.

CET1 reached 13.0% (+20bp), hitting the end-2027 target 18 months early - management's doctrine is now explicit ('13% is 13%'): any excess above 13% will be considered annually for additional distribution from 2027, on top of the 60% payout policy (50% dividend + 10% buyback, Q4 execution possible), with the next plan's payout 'clearly higher' (70% floated; CFO validates a potential 80-90% total-distribution logic if RWA growth stays disciplined). Interim dividend EUR 3.23 (50% of H1 EPS), paid 28 September.

CIB +13% driven by Global Markets +17% (Equity & Prime Services +43% on volatility AND structural share gains - #4 US structured products, ~9% APAC share; FICC flat on a high base, a relative lag vs US banks) and Securities Services +17%; Global Banking 'pivoted' with the +5% q/q RWA build presented as an early signal of a strong H2. Eurozone commercial banks + Personal Finance +8.2% with double-digit NII growth expected to extend 'well into 2030'; Arval remains the soft spot (used-car results; consensus still ~EUR 100M too high for H2 26 and again for 2027).

Cost momentum: support-function savings raised from EUR 700M to EUR 1B/year (EUR 15B addressable base, ~80% of IT/support savings already identified, ~25% delivered as early as 2027), accelerating cost/income improvement to ~2pts/year from 2027 - toward <56% in 2028 and ~50% by 2030 (2030 plan to be announced 2 February 2027 with a ~15% ROTE ambition); FY26 cost of risk kept <40bp (39bp in Q2 incl. EUR 95M geopolitical overlay) and Corporate Center loss guidance improved from EUR -1.4B to EUR -1.2B.

hypothese.summary: Large diversified French bank (CPBS, CIB, IPS) executing its 2024-2028 growth plan, with a Q2 26 well above expectations (attributable net income +33,4%) driven by equity markets and the AXA IM integration, a CET1 ratio already at the level of the 2027 target, and regular profitability/efficiency targets revised upwards in February 2026.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Largest eurozone bank by balance sheet, structured in three balanced poles (CPBS ~52% of revenue; CIB ~37%; IPS ~14%, boosted by AXA IM since 01/07/2025). The thesis is a disciplined mature banking compounder: ROTE rising from 11.6% (2025) toward the 12% 2026 target and the RAISED >13% 2028 target, cost-income falling toward <56% in 2028, EPS compounding >8%/yr on the GTS plan floor with buybacks shrinking the count -1.8%/yr. Q2 26 confirmed all objectives unchanged.

== THESIS READ ==
- The plan is tracking: FY25 landed at +0.2% above the EPS floor - the first measurable scorecard observation in the portfolio's bank universe. Watch: H2 cost-income progression toward <56%.
- Capital math is the buyback warranty: CET1 13.0% vs 10.43% SREP = 257bp headroom with the 13% target maintained - the projected accretion is now explicitly funded (capitalConstraint updated). Watch: Basel finalization impacts and the 2027 tranche authorization.
- The CFO's evoked post-2028 ~50% cost-income horizon is NOT in the model (stops at the <56%/2028 official target extended to ~53.5% by 2030). Watch: formalization at a future investor day - it would be upside.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Bank base: 'ca' = net banking income (PNB), 'ebit' = gross operating income (RBE), 'net' = published group net (RNPG); omniumND null by sector convention (deposits/CET1/MREL are not an industrial balance sheet). The bridge's 'other' line is the cost of risk (rising -3.3bn to -4.2bn with volume growth), minorities ~-820M, ETR 28% normative (26.5% actual 2025).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Revenue +5-6%/yr per plan; cost-income 58.5% (2026) -> ~53.5% (2030); RNPG +10.5%/yr 2026-2028 then ~7.5%; shares -1.8%/yr funded by the CET1 headroom; EPS 12.39 (2026) vs consensus 11.88 - Omnium sits above street but below the plan's own arithmetic. Watch: cost of risk vs the <40bp commitment; AXA IM synergies; French political/fiscal risk on the domestic franchise.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Oct); 2026 ROTE landing (Feb 2027) - first full plan-cycle verdict; 2027 buyback tranche; any post-2028 plan formalization.

ancrages.moteur: Official target confirmed at Q2 26: attributable net income growth >10%/yr on average over 2025-2028 (raised in February 2026 from a CAGR target of >7% over 2024-2026), ROTE >13% in 2028 (previous target 13%). Model assumption: 10,5%/yr over 2026-2028 (a slight premium vs the official floor), then a slowdown to 8%/7,5% in 2029-2030 in the absence of an official target beyond 2028 (high confidence on 2026-2028, low on 2029-2030).

Official cost/income ratio target <56% in 2028 (raised from ~58%), against 61,2% in 2025 and already 56,7% in Q2 26 alone - decline trajectory modelled gradually over 2026-2028 then continuing moderately over 2029-2030.

EXPLICIT USER INSTRUCTION: distribution raised to a 70% payout of net income from 2027 (55% dividend + 15% buybacks), against the officially confirmed policy of 60% minimum from 2027 (50% dividend minimum + the remainder, further detail expected at the 2027-2030 CMD of February 2027) and 60% in 2026 (50% dividend + 10% buybacks, this last year kept in line with the official policy). Assumption explicitly more generous than the official floor known to date (user instruction not yet officially confirmed by management beyond the 60% floor).

CET1 at 13,0% at 30/06/2026, already at the level of the 2027 target, well above SREP requirements (10,43%) - the distribution of the excess CET1 above 13% will be determined annually from 2027 (not quantified at this stage, potential additional distribution not modelled in the 70%/55%/15% retained) (high confidence on the occurrence, none on the amount).

Cost of risk kept below the 40 basis point target in 2025-2026 (36bp in 2025, 39bp in Q2 26, including 95 M€ of additional provisioning for the geopolitical environment) - assumption of stability around 35-38bp over the projection horizon, with no major macro deterioration built in.

AXA IM integration (consolidated since 1 July 2025): revenue and cost synergies estimated at 550 M€ pre-tax by 2029, integration costs of 690 M€ (of which ~400 M€ in 2026) - gradual ramp-up of the net synergies embedded in the net banking income/gross operating income trajectory for 2026-2029, with no dedicated separate line.

Disposal gain on the 25% stake in AG Insurance sold to Ageas (~850 M€, transaction completed on 28 April 2026, booked in Q2 26) treated as a genuine one-off and excluded from omniumNet (and from Q2 26 in quarterlyEPS); only the recurring annual effect estimated at ~+40 M€/yr (linked to the increase in the Ageas stake to ~22,5% and to the move to equity-method accounting) is retained in the base from 2026.

'Sudan' litigation still ongoing: the Bank was found liable at first instance (20,5 M$, October 2025) and was granted leave to appeal (decision of 8 January 2026), motion filed in early February 2026, BNP Paribas says it is confident in the strength of its arguments - legal risk not quantified, not provisioned in the adjXXX beyond the amount already paid, potential extension of the plaintiff class raised by their lawyers (high confidence on the occurrence, none on the outcome).

Projections use 28% normative with 'other' as the fitted cost-of-risk line (rising -3.3bn to -4.2bn with loan-book growth). finNet=0 by construction (no net-debt concept for a bank).
